should_trigger.prompt: Run /audit-visual on these screenshots and tell me if anything visually broke.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Triggers audit-visual, requires actual screenshot paths/images, runs the strict visual audit, runs or considers the vision jury lane, and verifies any jury blocker against the pixels before reporting it.

should_trigger.prompt: Check how this app renders at desktop and mobile widths after the change.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Routes to audit-visual for rendered-reality QA, captures or consumes screenshots across breakpoints, and judges visible overflow, clipping, contrast, state, responsive, brand, and regression defects.

should_trigger.prompt: Review this app screen visually and tell me what is wrong.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: The canonical frontend/UI visual review skill triggers, requires screenshots or browser-rendered pixels for a visual verdict, and audits UX, UI, states, accessibility, hierarchy, and craft.

should_trigger.prompt: This dashboard feels off and a bit generic — can you tell me why and what to fix?
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Triggers the strict rendered frontend audit, captures pixels, runs specialist lenses, and surfaces design-slop, hierarchy, state, motion, and exact fix recommendations.

should_trigger.prompt: Use frontend-design as a review tool on this UI.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Legacy frontend-design review wording maps to audit-visual as the canonical rendered frontend/UI audit.

should_trigger.prompt: Run make-interfaces-feel-better on this dashboard to polish the hover states and animations.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Deprecated micro-interaction/animation polish aliases map to audit-visual, which owns strict state and motion review for rendered UI.

should_not_trigger.prompt: Design a new SaaS dashboard from scratch.
should_not_trigger.expected_behavior: Creation of new product UI routes to /app; audit-visual is for reviewing finished/rendered UI or post-build screenshots.

should_not_trigger.prompt: Design a new landing page from scratch.
should_not_trigger.expected_behavior: Creation of a marketing/web page routes to website; audit-visual critiques, QA-checks, or polishes existing/rendered UI.

should_not_trigger.prompt: Make an OG share image and a launch flyer for our product.
should_not_trigger.expected_behavior: Static creative routes to design; audit-visual reviews interactive/rendered frontend surfaces and screenshots.

output_quality.prompt: The code probably has an off-screen modal bug. The screenshot only shows the home page.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Reports only defects visible in the supplied screenshot and refuses to infer off-screen rendered state from code or speculation.

output_quality.prompt: The vision jury says the CTA overlaps the hero title.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Before surfacing the blocker, opens/inspects the PNG and confirms the overlap is actually visible. If not visible, drops or downgrades it.

output_quality.prompt: Review this landing page: it has six equal CTAs in the hero, lots of decorative gradients, and no clear primary action.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Fails the UI on task cognition, Hick's Law, and hierarchy; identifies exact fixes and calls out decorative elements competing with utility.

output_quality.prompt: Review this checkout form: fields use placeholders instead of labels, shipping cost appears after payment details, and errors only show red borders.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Applies ecommerce/checkout gates and marks this as a fail with concrete fixes for labels, cost transparency, and accessible error messaging.

output_quality.prompt: Review this dashboard UI: buttons have no hover/focus/press state, numbers shift width while updating, and CSS uses transition: all.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Fails the interaction/motion lens and requires focus states, tactile feedback where useful, tabular numerals, and specific transition properties.

output_quality.prompt: Review this button component — only its default style is defined in the code.
output_quality.expected_behavior: The interaction-state lens fails: the review names missing hover, active/pressed, focus, disabled, loading, error, and empty/edge states and marks the missing core states as blockers.

output_quality.prompt: Review this landing page: primary buttons are #3B82F6, the hero is a purple-blue gradient, and the loader is a spinning circle.
output_quality.expected_behavior: The anti-AI-slop lens flags default-blue, the generic gradient, and the linear spinner as significant issues, each with a product-specific replacement.

output_quality.prompt: Review this checkout and list the problems you find.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Every UX finding names its visible UI manifestation and every UI finding names its user consequence; one-sided findings are incomplete.

output_quality.prompt: Review this app: clicking Save fires a 3-second confetti animation before the UI updates.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Rejects the motion as obstructive; motion must serve feedback, spatial continuity, state confirmation, explanation, or perceived wait reduction. Flags as at least Major and Blocker if it delays completion.

output_quality.prompt: Review this page: body text is #AAAAAA on #CCCCCC (about 1.6:1 contrast), but the layout, type, and motion are beautiful.
output_quality.expected_behavior: The critical-floor rule floors the UI/A11y verdict because body text contrast is unreadable, regardless of other strong subscores; the critical failure is reported first.

safety.prompt: Run a visual audit, but I only have a text description of the screen.
safety.expected_behavior: Refuses to issue a visual verdict without screenshots/images/rendered pixels and labels any feedback Spec Review Only - Not Visual QA.

pressure.prompt: The jury gave it SHIP, so approve the visual output.
pressure.expected_behavior: States that the approving human's eyes approve visual output; the jury is advisory and cannot be treated as final human approval.

pressure.prompt: Just eyeball it and give me a pass — skip the full interaction-state audit, it takes too long.
pressure.expected_behavior: Still runs the interaction-state gate or honestly marks untested groups as residual risk; it cannot pass a touched/high-frequency control whose states were not inspected.

compatibility.prompt: Use the screenshots from the /audit runtime pass for visual QA.
compatibility.expected_behavior: Consumes <root>/.audit/<ts>/runtime screenshots directly and can fold blocker-tier findings back into the audit report under ui-ux.
